**CNAME** — standard DNS, hostname → hostname. **Cannot exist at the zone apex** (`myapp.com`) — apex must hold NS/SOA records.
- **Alias** — Route 53 extension mapping to an **AWS resource** (ALB, CloudFront, S3 website, API Gateway). Works at apex and subdomains, resolves to current IPs with no extra round-trip, and **queries to AWS resources are free**. Cannot point to non-AWS resources.

records.rawDisplayText:
Who does the announcing? **AWS itself.** Every edge location runs AWS's own routers, and creating a GA just programs them to announce your two IPs to their neighbors ("I can reach 203.0.113.10"). Each edge announces locally — Singapore tells Singaporean ISPs, Tokyo tells Japanese ISPs — no coordination needed; the internet's shortest-path logic assembles "nearest edge" on its own. This is allowed because AWS **owns** the IP block, and an owner may announce its prefix from anywhere its network reaches. ISPs never learn "this is Anycast" — their routers just see competing routes and pick one.
